summary:
Technical re-review of rework-4, iteration 2 (sub-mv3ussgo-0158904e, responding to rev-mv3ua9lc-01c4624b). Only two files changed since iteration 1: 006_autoincrement_ids.sql (the sequence floor, and the extractions/requirements rebuild) and migrate-006.test.js. All ten artifacts match the submission's sha256 (ev:ev-mv3uuxsy-01e2b908). Coverage across all three handoffs: 9 declared, 9 changed, 9 submitted, 0 undeclared (ev:ev-mv3v5xoc-01f38485). The security draft rework-4-security-2.md (FINAL: SEC-RW4-1 resolved; no new blocking, major or minor finding; new info SEC-RW4-I6) is folded in.

SEC-RW4-1 is resolved, verified by me.
- **Code:** before the staging tables are dropped, 006 creates any missing sqlite_sequence row and raises each sequence to the highest id still named. The sources are: audit entity ids (request, image, plan_version), the plan.create details planVersionId and runId, the extraction.run detail extractionId, and the staged model_spend.request_id. Each detail read is guarded by json_valid. I checked against the code that the app writes exactly these keys: extraction.js L509-L510, plans.js L259-L263.
- **The header comment and safety point 6 are corrected.**
- **The new RS-39 test** deletes X's ids on 005, before the upgrade. It fails on the previous 006 (engineer ev:ev-mv3udofz-01b7eb42; my P1 with 12 of 21 failing).
- **My re-check on the current 006 (ev:ev-mv3v55rb-01a9eca2):**
  - S1, my iteration-1 scenario: Y now gets 3/12/102/31/8 instead of 2/11/101/30/7, and none of X's audit rows sits on Y's ids.
  - S2: with every table empty at the upgrade, audit-named ids are still not reissued.
  - S3: the upgraded schema equals a fresh one, the triggers fire, and the foreign keys of extractions and requirements are intact.
  - My unchanged iteration-1 script now fails its 'reproduces' expectation, as intended: ev:ev-mv3v562s-0146e998 (reproduction, not cited as passing).
- **Falsification (ev:ev-mv3v5pr0-01e44852):** the control is green, 42/42. All 12 mutants are killed:
  - each of the 7 floor sources removed, one at a time;
  - the json_valid guard removed;
  - extractions not restored;
  - requirements without AUTOINCREMENT;
  - the extractions_request index dropped.
  Removing the defensive 'create missing sequence rows' INSERT is an equivalent mutant on SQLite 3.50.4: an INSERT ... SELECT into an AUTOINCREMENT table creates its row even when it copies nothing. Keeping the INSERT is right.

Declared checks:
- Green set from ho-mv3um18e-0136c6a3, verbatim: 131/131 (ev:ev-mv3uuxia-01d15eee).
- npm test, first run: 2087 tests, 2078 pass, 1 fail, 8 skipped (ev:ev-mv3uxnxc-01a9d1b7). The failure is the uploads-retention timer test at line 711. Per dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152 I re-ran once: 2087 tests, 2079 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped, 0 todo; ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 (ev:ev-mv3uzh3f-018fafca).
- npm run test:browser on the live tree: 8/10 (ev:ev-mv3v15lw-01fc58b9). Both failures are e6's cross-site journey, waiting for [data-testid=paypal-returned]. e5's in-progress reset edit to public/js/views/request-detail.js (snapshot 7ecc085) now hides that notice. On a scratch copy with only that file taken from e470ce7 and every rework-4 file as submitted, the suite passes 10/10 (ev:ev-mv3v26ts-01bed266). I attribute the red to e5/e6 (TR-R4-10).

Decision: approve.
- TR-R4-1 (minor) remains, documented by dec-mv3u4zzu-01f07c5a; its resolution is a README and verification-report item.
- Info items carried with owners: TR-R4-3, TR-R4-4 (extended by SEC-RW4-I6), TR-R4-6, TR-R4-9, TR-R4-10, SEC-RW4-I2, SEC-RW4-I4, SEC-RW4-I6.
- Resolved: SEC-RW4-1, SEC-RW4-I1, TR-R4-8.

criteria.description: FU-23 and SEC-R-1: ids never reused; general limit fails open on busy reads
criteria.notes:
FU-23 holds on both paths.
- **Fresh databases and deletes after the upgrade:** iteration-1 tests and mutants, still green.
- **Ids hard-deleted on 005 before the upgrade:** the sequence floor; see S1 and S2 of my re-check and the security reviewer's app-level probe.

Why the floor's sources are complete for what the app writes:
- Request ids are always named by request.create.
- Images are named by their upload and retention audit rows.
- Plan versions and runs are named by plan.create (and plan.approve).
- Extractions are named by extraction.run.
- The other planVersionId detail keys (orders, reservations) belong to plan versions that can never be hard-deleted, because a request with orders or reservations is only tombstoned.

Requirements ids deleted on 005 can be reissued, but nothing names them (disclosed; the security reviewer confirmed it is unobservable).

The extractions/requirements rebuild: rows are preserved, the table text is 002's plus the keyword, and the index, foreign keys and fresh-schema equality hold. X1, X2 and X3 are killed.

SEC-R-1 is unchanged since my iteration-1 resolution (general-limit.js, rbac.js and their tests are byte-identical).

The migrate-006 test changes weaken no assertion. The seeded test now expects the floored sequences, and the dangling spend pointer is parameterised per test.

criteria.description: Phase D review rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56 TR-D-3 and security draft: rescue_requests, plan_versions, images and planning_runs use INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so after a hard delete of the highest id the next row reuses it and audit rows or a model_spend row point at another customer's request; migration 006 rebuilds those tables with AUTOINCREMENT (app-only, data preserved), model_spend.request_id gets a foreign key or check, and an RS-39 test shows no id is reused. Rework-1 review SEC-R-1: src/auth/general-limit.js takes the write lock on every signed-in call; GET and HEAD fail open on a busy error (the request proceeds uncounted and the event is logged), with a lock-holder test. Only b1 and c1 (approved) owned these files. Required before e4.
The rework's not-applicable decision on mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 holds
criteria.notes: The third claim edits only a SQL migration and its unit test. The rework's nine files contain no tool-call guard, pre-commit hook or root discovery. The lesson's 'Applies when' conditions do not hold. Not applicable.

findings.title: Migration 006's run time grows quadratically with plan versions (about 9 s at 5000 request trees under the write lock); documented, not optimised
findings.detail:
Measured in iteration 1 (ev:ev-mv3tpe9a-016d484a). Decision dec-mv3u4zzu-01f07c5a keeps 006 without temporary indexes. The cost and the rule (upgrade with one process, before traffic) go into the README and the verification report.

The floor adds 6 aggregate queries over audit_events and model_spend. That is linear and negligible next to the plan_versions rebuild.
findings.recommendation: Owner: g2 (README) and the orchestrator (verification report), per dec-mv3u4zzu-01f07c5a. Resolved when both state the measured cost (about 1 s at 2000 and 9 s at 5000 request trees, growing quadratically) and the single-process upgrade rule.

findings.title: (security) the floor reads only the audit sources the app writes; the corrected safety point 6 claims slightly more
findings.detail: From rework-4-security-2.md. The floor is bypassed only by inputs the app cannot write: ids named only in malformed JSON, a request id named only in another entity's detail, or absurd values (ev:ev-mv3v0chb-01c75520, GAP lines). Point 6 reads 'no id that audit_events or model_spend still names'. That is true for the rows the app writes, not for every detail key. I agree, and I also checked the detail keys the app writes against the floor's sources.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator (verification report). Resolved when the report words the guarantee as 'no id named by the audit rows the app writes for these tables (request, image and plan_version entities; plan.create planVersionId and runId; extraction.run extractionId) or by model_spend'. No code change.

findings.title: The verification report must state the SET NULL behaviour of model_spend and the NULLing of dangling pointers at the upgrade
findings.detail: Carried from rev-mv3ua9lc-01c4624b. The rows stay for the daily budget with request_id NULL. The floor still reads the original pointers from the staged copy, so a nulled pointer never lets its old request id be reissued (F1 is killed).
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator (verification report). Resolved when the report states it, together with SEC-RW4-I6's wording.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
Condition met.
- **The floor:** before the staging tables are dropped, 006 creates any missing sqlite_sequence row and raises each rebuilt table's sequence to the highest id still named. The sources are the audit request, image and plan_version entities; plan.create planVersionId and runId; extraction.run extractionId; and the staged model_spend.request_id (json_valid-guarded).
- **Comments:** the L20 comment (now L21-L28) and safety point 6 are corrected. Point 6's wording is refined by SEC-RW4-I6.
- **The test:** the new RS-39 test deletes X's highest request, image, extraction, run and plan version on 005 before migrating. It shows larger ids for Y and none of X's audit rows on them. Seven per-source cases cover each source.
- **Failing first:** on the previous 006 (engineer ev:ev-mv3udofz-01b7eb42; my P1, 12 of 21 failing).
- **Mutants:** each of the seven source mutants is killed.
- **My scenario re-run:** 3/12/102/31/8 instead of 2/11/101/30/7. Empty tables are also covered.
- **The security reviewer's app-level probe:** Y gets 6/5/5/6/6, and Y's timeline shows only Y's events.
- **Checks:** the green set, npm test (re-run) and the browser suite (attributed) pass.

Resolved.
- extractions and requirements are rebuilt with AUTOINCREMENT, the table text otherwise equal to 002, and the extractions_request index is recreated.
- After a delete following the upgrade, the next ids are 701/701.
- extractions also gets the floor from extraction.run extractionId.
- requirements ids deleted on 005 above the surviving maximum can still be reissued, but nothing names them (disclosed; unobservable per security).
- My mutants X1, X2 and X3 are killed. S3 shows fresh-schema equality and intact foreign keys.

Resolved by decision dec-mv3u4zr4-0165c54d: phase:e-payments is submitted only after phase:rework-4 is approved, and the phase E reviewers re-run the suite with both landed. Run 2 of npm test on this tree (e4's completed code plus rework-4) is green.
